scope: Adult cigarette smoking cessation; UK research prototype; no prescribing
publication_rule: Patient-facing retrieval MUST require status VERIFIED. This candidate catalogue contains no VERIFIED records.

records.title: Tobacco: preventing uptake, promoting quitting and treating dependence
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
records.population: People in the UK covered by tobacco prevention and dependence treatment recommendations
records.intervention_or_exposure: Tobacco prevention, quitting and dependence treatment
records.main_finding: NG209 is the current UK-first guideline for this prototype and was updated after review of cytisinicline evidence.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Current UK guidance describes several ways adults can get support to stop smoking.
limitations: A guideline recommendation is not an individual prediction.
Local availability may differ.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Use NICE methods and linked evidence reviews; do not assign a trial-style risk-of-bias rating to the guideline itself.

numeric_claims.claim: Published 30 November 2021 and last updated 4 February 2025.

records.title: NG209 recommendations 1.12.2 and 1.12.6: accessible interventions and behavioural support
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
records.population: Adults who smoke
records.intervention_or_exposure: Behavioural support, NRT, cytisinicline, varenicline, bupropion, nicotine-containing e-cigarettes, and named seminar option
records.main_finding: Adults should have access to a range of behavioural and product options; behavioural support should be offered with stop-smoking options subject to the guideline exception.
records.patient_friendly_summary: There is more than one evidence-based way to get help with stopping smoking.
limitations: Does not determine personal suitability or local availability.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Recommendation-level record; independently match exact wording before promotion.

records.title: NG209 recommendations 1.12.8 and 1.12.9: relative likelihood of successful stopping
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
records.population: Adults who smoke and use an option with behavioural support
records.intervention_or_exposure: Cytisinicline, combination NRT, varenicline, or nicotine-containing e-cigarettes
records.comparator: Bupropion or a single form of NRT, all with behavioural support
records.effect_value: More likely versus less likely groups
records.main_finding: NICE places cytisinicline, combination short- and long-acting NRT, varenicline, and nicotine-containing e-cigarettes in the more-likely-to-succeed group when combined with behavioural support.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Some options have stronger evidence than others, especially when used with behavioural support.
limitations: Not a head-to-head league table.
Does not establish personal suitability.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Do not translate the qualitative recommendation into a numerical ranking.

records.title: NG209 recommendation 1.12.11: nicotine and smoking-related harm
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
records.population: People who smoke considering licensed stop-smoking products
records.main_finding: Most smoking-related health problems are caused by other components in tobacco smoke, not nicotine; licensed nicotine-containing products carry much lower risks than smoking.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Nicotine drives dependence, but most smoking-related damage comes from tobacco smoke.
limitations: Does not mean nicotine is harmless or suitable for everyone.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Keep wording close to NICE and avoid universal safety claims.

records.title: NG209 harm-reduction approaches for people not ready to stop in one go
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
records.population: People who smoke and are not ready to stop in one go
records.intervention_or_exposure: Cutting down before stopping, smoking reduction, or temporary abstinence
records.main_finding: NICE supports structured harm-reduction approaches, ideally linked to stopping completely.
records.patient_friendly_summary: If you are not ready to stop in one go, you can still choose a structured step towards stopping.
limitations: Reducing is not equivalent to stopping completely.
Do not promise proportional health-risk reduction.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Separate behavioural recommendation from claims about clinical outcomes.

records.title: Nicotine vaping in England: 2022 evidence update main findings
authors: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities commissioned review team
records.organisation: OHID, Department of Health and Social Care
records.population: People who vape, smoke, both, or neither
records.comparator: Cigarette smoking and no nicotine use
records.outcome: Short-, medium-, and long-term health risk
records.timeframe: Short and medium term; limited long-term evidence
records.main_finding: Vaping poses a small fraction of smoking risks in the short and medium term, is not risk-free, and has unresolved long-term uncertainty.
records.patient_friendly_summary: For adults who smoke, switching completely to a nicotine vape is likely much less harmful than continuing to smoke, but vaping is not risk-free.
limitations: Long-term evidence is limited.
Product and use patterns vary.
Do not express as a precise personal percentage.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Independent reviewer should check for a post-2022 OHID replacement review.

records.title: MPFT Health and Wellbeing Resources: quitting smoking and local services
authors: Midlands Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
records.population: People seeking health and wellbeing resources in MPFT areas
records.intervention_or_exposure: Local and national stop-smoking service signposting
records.timeframe: Current contact details at check date
records.main_finding: MPFT hosts public quit-smoking information and links to local services across several areas.
records.patient_friendly_summary: This page can help you find local and national stop-smoking support.
limitations: Not an effectiveness study.
Eligibility, phone numbers, and providers can change.
Does not imply prototype endorsement.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Treat as a resource record, never outcome evidence.

numeric_claims.claim: The page describes the Staffordshire service as available to residents aged 18 or over.
numeric_claims.source_locator: Staffordshire section of the MPFT resource page

records.title: MPFT visitor guidance: smoke-free trust
authors: Midlands Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
records.population: Visitors to MPFT sites
records.main_finding: MPFT publicly states that it is a totally smoke-free trust.
records.patient_friendly_summary: MPFT sites are smoke free.
limitations: Not clinical effectiveness evidence.
Does not imply endorsement of this prototype.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Resource/policy record only.

records.title: Benefits of quitting smoking
records.population: People who smoke
records.comparator: Continuing smoking or never smoking, depending on claim
records.outcome: Heart attack and lung cancer mortality risk milestones
records.relative_effect: Heart-attack risk half at 1 year; lung-cancer death risk half at 10 years; heart-attack risk similar to never-smoker at 15 years
records.main_finding: NHS presents a simple long-term recovery timeline after stopping smoking.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Health benefits build over time after you stop smoking.
limitations: Underlying studies are not exposed on the page.
Milestones are not exact personal predictions.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Citation verifier must trace every milestone before promotion.

numeric_claims.claim: After 1 year, risk of heart attack halves compared with a smoker's.
numeric_claims.source_locator: NHS Better Health benefits page, Reduced risks section

numeric_claims.claim: After 10 years, risk of death from lung cancer falls to half that of a smoker.
numeric_claims.source_locator: NHS Better Health benefits page, Reduced risks section

numeric_claims.claim: After 15 years, risk of heart attack falls to the same as someone who has never smoked.
numeric_claims.source_locator: NHS Better Health benefits page, Reduced risks section

records.title: NHS stop smoking services help you quit
records.population: People who use treatment plus an NHS stop-smoking service
records.main_finding: The page reports a large benefit from combining treatment and specialist support, but the exact evidence basis is not shown and its review date has passed.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Specialist support and treatment can improve the chance of stopping.
limitations: Comparator and timeframe unclear.
Underlying citation not exposed.
Page is past its displayed next review date.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Do not publish the multiplier without primary provenance.

numeric_claims.claim: Treatment plus support from an NHS Stop Smoking Service makes a person up to 3 times more likely to stop for good.
numeric_claims.source_locator: NHS service page, one-to-one and group sessions section

records.title: Behavioural interventions for smoking cessation: an overview and network meta-analysis
records.study_design: Systematic review of reviews and component network meta-analysis
records.population: Adults who smoke
records.outcome: Smoking abstinence at 6 months or longer
records.main_finding: Counselling improves long-term smoking cessation, with high-certainty evidence.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Talking support can improve the chance of staying stopped.
limitations: Odds ratios are not the same as risk ratios.
Absolute effect varies by baseline quit rate and support context.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Review reported benefit remained after removing studies at high risk of bias.

numeric_claims.claim: Counselling OR 1.44, 95% CrI 1.22 to 1.70; 194 studies; 72,273 participants.

records.title: Combined pharmacotherapy and behavioural interventions for smoking cessation
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
records.population: People who smoke, mainly recruited in healthcare settings
records.sample_size: 19,488 participants in 52 pooled studies after excluding an atypical outlier
records.comparator: Usual care, brief advice, or less intensive behavioural support
records.main_finding: Combining pharmacotherapy and behavioural support improves long-term cessation versus minimal support/usual care.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Stop-smoking products work best as part of a supported quit attempt.
limitations: Most studies used NRT and older service models.
Comparator is not medicine alone.
Check for a newer synthesis.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: One atypically intensive study was excluded from the principal pooled estimate; moderate heterogeneity remained.

numeric_claims.claim: RR 1.83, 95% CI 1.68 to 1.98; 52 studies; 19,488 participants; I-squared 36%.

records.title: Nicotine replacement therapy versus control for smoking cessation
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
records.population: People making a quit attempt
records.main_finding: Licensed NRT forms improve long-term cessation compared with placebo or no NRT.
records.patient_friendly_summary: NRT can reduce cravings and improve the chance of stopping.
limitations: Does not select an NRT for an individual.
Absolute effect varies by context.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: High-quality evidence as reported by review; independently confirm current version.

numeric_claims.claim: Any NRT versus control RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.49 to 1.61.

records.title: Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
records.population: People using NRT to stop smoking
records.intervention_or_exposure: Combination NRT: patch plus fast-acting NRT
records.main_finding: Combination NRT improves long-term quit rates compared with a single form, with high-certainty evidence.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Using a patch with a fast-acting NRT can work better than using one form alone.
limitations: Does not determine individual product, dose, or contraindications.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: High-certainty evidence as reported by review.

numeric_claims.claim: Combination NRT versus single form RR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17 to 1.37; 16 studies; 12,169 participants.

records.title: Nicotine receptor partial agonists for smoking cessation: varenicline effects
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
records.population: Adults who smoke and want to stop
records.main_finding: Varenicline improves cessation versus placebo and versus single-form NRT.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Varenicline is an effective stop-smoking medicine, but a clinician or pharmacist must assess whether it is suitable for you.
limitations: No personal prescribing or suitability advice.
Serious-adverse-event estimates require careful presentation.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Review reported high-certainty cessation evidence; medication harms require separate verification.

numeric_claims.claim: Varenicline versus placebo RR 2.32, 95% CI 2.15 to 2.51; 41 studies; 17,395 participants.
Varenicline versus single-form NRT RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.14 to 1.37; 11 studies; 7,572 participants.

records.title: Nicotine receptor partial agonists for smoking cessation: cytisine/cytisinicline effects
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
records.population: Adults who smoke and want to stop
records.main_finding: Cytisine/cytisinicline improves cessation versus placebo; direct comparison with varenicline was imprecise and found no clear difference.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Cytisinicline is an evidence-based stop-smoking medicine; ask a stop-smoking adviser, pharmacist, or GP about current access and suitability.
limitations: Substantial heterogeneity.
Direct varenicline comparison is low certainty.
No personal prescribing advice.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Moderate-certainty efficacy versus placebo; I-squared 83%; low-certainty head-to-head evidence.

numeric_claims.claim: Cytisine versus placebo RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.47; 4 studies; 4,623 participants; I-squared 83%.
Cytisine versus varenicline RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.26; 2 studies; 2,131 participants.

records.title: Electronic cigarettes for smoking cessation
records.population: Adults who smoke
records.sample_size: 2,544 participants in 7 studies for nicotine e-cigarette versus NRT pooled estimate
records.main_finding: Nicotine e-cigarettes increase cessation compared with NRT, with high-certainty efficacy evidence; serious-adverse-event evidence remains less certain.
records.patient_friendly_summary: For adults who smoke, nicotine vapes can help some people stop smoking. They are not risk-free and long-term effects remain less certain.
limitations: Living review may update frequently.
Long-term safety is not established by cessation trials.
Included regulated nicotine products; products vary.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: High-certainty efficacy comparison versus NRT; low-certainty serious-adverse-event evidence.

numeric_claims.claim: Nicotine e-cigarette versus NRT RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.93; 7 studies; 2,544 participants.
Absolute difference 4 additional quitters per 100, 95% CI 2 to 6.

records.title: Smoking cessation for improving mental health
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis, mainly observational comparisons within cessation studies
records.population: People who stopped smoking compared with people who continued, including mental-health subpopulations
records.outcome: Anxiety, depression, mixed symptoms, stress, affect, and quality of life
records.main_finding: Mental health does not appear to worsen after stopping and may improve, but certainty varies and confounding is important.
records.patient_friendly_summary: After the withdrawal period, stopping smoking does not appear to make mental health worse on average and may improve mood and anxiety.
limitations: Not evidence that quitting treats an individual's mental illness.
Serious risk of time-varying confounding.
Certainty ranges from very low to moderate.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: All studies were deemed at serious risk of bias from possible time-varying confounding; some depression studies were at critical risk.

numeric_claims.claim: 102 studies representing more than 169,500 participants.
Anxiety SMD -0.28, 95% CI -0.43 to -0.13; 15 studies; 3,141 participants; low certainty.
Depression SMD -0.30, 95% CI -0.39 to -0.21; 34 studies; 7,156 participants; very low certainty.

records.title: Relapse prevention interventions for smoking cessation
records.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised and quasi-randomised trials
records.population: People who had recently stopped smoking or were in cessation programmes
records.intervention_or_exposure: Behavioural relapse-prevention add-ons or extended pharmacotherapy
records.comparator: No additional relapse-prevention intervention or standard duration
records.effect_measure: Risk ratio for selected pharmacotherapy analysis
records.relative_effect: Extended varenicline improved maintained abstinence in selected assisted abstainers
records.main_finding: Generic behavioural relapse-prevention add-ons did not show worthwhile benefit; selected extended pharmacotherapy evidence was more promising.
records.patient_friendly_summary: A lapse does not erase progress. The coach can help you learn from it, but should not claim that generic coping advice is proven to prevent relapse.
limitations: Older review.
Medication-duration findings must not be turned into prescribing advice.
High heterogeneity for extended varenicline.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Only 6 studies were rated low risk of bias overall; extended varenicline evidence moderate certainty with I-squared 82%.

numeric_claims.claim: 81 studies and 69,094 participants overall.
Extended varenicline RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.41; 2 studies; 1,297 participants; I-squared 82%.

records.title: Mortality in relation to smoking: 50 years' observations on male British doctors
records.population: Male British doctors
records.sample_size: 34,439 male British doctors in the original cohort
records.intervention_or_exposure: Stopping cigarette smoking at different ages
records.effect_measure: Approximate years of life expectancy gained
records.effect_value: 3, 6, 9, or 10 years when stopping at about 60, 50, 40, or 30
records.absolute_effect: Approximate years gained in this cohort
records.main_finding: Stopping was associated with substantial longevity benefit even at older ages.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Stopping at any age can bring important health benefits; earlier stopping brings more benefit on average.
limitations: Historical cohort of male doctors.
Observational evidence.
Not an individual life-expectancy calculator.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Healthy-worker/professional cohort and historical smoking patterns limit transportability.

numeric_claims.claim: Stopping at about ages 60, 50, 40, or 30 was associated with about 3, 6, 9, or 10 years of life expectancy gained, respectively.

records.title: Association of smoking cessation with subsequent risk of cardiovascular disease
records.population: Framingham original and offspring cohorts; principal analysis of heavy ever-smokers and never-smokers
records.comparator: Current heavy smoking; separately never smoking
records.timeframe: Within 5 years; residual risk over 10 to 15 years and beyond
records.confidence_interval: 95% CI 0.49 to 0.76 for quitting within 5 years versus current smoking
records.absolute_effect: 6.94 versus 11.56 events per 1,000 person-years; adjusted difference -4.51
records.relative_effect: Lower CVD risk versus continuing smoking
records.main_finding: CVD risk was lower within 5 years of cessation than with continued heavy smoking, while residual excess versus never-smokers could persist for years.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Heart and circulation benefits can begin within the first years after stopping, while some past-smoking risk may remain.
limitations: Observational US cohort.
Principal estimates concern heavy ever-smokers.
Cohorts disagreed on time to approach never-smoker risk.
Not an individual prediction.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Adjusted for measured confounders, but residual confounding and self-reported smoking remain possible.

numeric_claims.claim: Within 5 years of quitting versus current smoking: HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.76.
numeric_claims.source_locator: JAMA article, results paragraph and Table 3

numeric_claims.claim: Incidence rates 6.94 versus 11.56 per 1,000 person-years; difference -4.51, 95% CI -5.90 to -2.77.
numeric_claims.source_locator: JAMA article, results paragraph and Table 3

records.title: Smoking cessation and lung function in mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the Lung Health Study
records.organisation: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
records.study_design: Randomised cessation intervention study with observational comparison by sustained smoking status
records.population: Smokers with mild-to-moderate airway obstruction
records.outcome: Annual decline in FEV1 after the first year
records.absolute_effect: Approximately half the decline among sustained quitters
records.main_finding: Sustained quitters had substantially slower lung-function decline than continuing smokers after an initial improvement.
records.patient_friendly_summary: For people with airflow obstruction, stopping smoking can slow further loss of lung function.
limitations: Mild-to-moderate obstruction population.
Sustained-quit status was not the original randomised comparison.
Not applicable as an individual spirometry forecast.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Selection into sustained quitting may confound the smoking-status comparison despite randomised intervention allocation.

numeric_claims.claim: 3,926 smokers randomised; 3,818 with analyzable results.
Annual FEV1 decline 31 +/- 48 mL among sustained quitters versus 62 +/- 55 mL among continuing smokers.

records.title: Relation of active, passive, and quitting smoking with incident type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.population: Adults in prospective cohorts
records.sample_size: 88 studies; 5,898,795 participants; 295,446 incident type 2 diabetes cases
records.intervention_or_exposure: Current smoking, former smoking, and time since quitting
records.comparator: Non-smoking or never smoking, depending on analysis
records.timeframe: Less than 5 years, 5 to 9 years, and 10 years or longer since quitting
records.confidence_interval: Current smoking versus non-smoking 95% CI 1.33 to 1.42
records.relative_effect: Higher incident diabetes risk with current smoking; non-linear pattern after quitting
records.main_finding: Smoking was associated with higher diabetes incidence; recent quitters also had elevated observed risk that diminished with time, so simplistic immediate-risk-reduction claims are inappropriate.
records.patient_friendly_summary: Smoking is relevant to diabetes risk. Stopping remains important, but diabetes risk changes over time and cannot be predicted exactly from this evidence.
limitations: Observational evidence.
Residual confounding and weight change may explain part of the post-cessation pattern.
Do not imply quitting causes net health harm.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Prospective cohorts reduce recall bias but cannot remove residual confounding or reverse causation.

numeric_claims.claim: 88 studies; 5,898,795 participants; 295,446 incident cases.
Current smoking versus non-smoking RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.33 to 1.42.
Compared with never smoking: less than 5 years since quitting RR 1.54 (1.36 to 1.74), 5 to 9 years RR 1.18 (1.07 to 1.29), and 10 years or longer RR 1.11 (1.02 to 1.20).

records.title: Deterministic financial estimate policy
records.population: Prototype users who choose to enter cigarette price information
records.main_finding: Financial estimates should use user-entered prices and deterministic arithmetic, never a national average presented as personal fact.
records.patient_friendly_summary: This is an estimate based on the price and pack size you entered.
limitations: Does not capture discounts, switching products, partial cigarettes, or unreported purchases.
records.risk_of_bias_notes: Not an evidence claim; verify code with unit tests and show assumptions in the UI.
